findings.title: queued timestamp is fixed at import, not per assignment
findings.body: AssignmentSource.queued uses timezone.now() as a dataclass field default. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class is defined, not on each instance, so every AssignmentSource that does not pass queued shares one timestamp: the time this module was imported (the worker/web process start under a preload). The field is then copied into every outbound task payload via to_dict(). Rapid assignee changes, which this PR is meant to disambiguate, all get the same queued time, and any later staleness or ordering check on queued cannot tell them apart. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now). The new tests only assert queued is not None, so they do not catch the shared value.

findings.title: Task payload includes a raw datetime and will not round-trip
findings.body: to_dict() is asdict(self), so assignment_source_dict contains a live datetime under queued. That dict is the Celery kwargs for sync_assignee_outbound (sync.py, the apply_async call). Other arguments on this task are JSON primitives; a JSON Celery serializer raises TypeError when publishing a datetime, so the inbound webhook path (the only caller that sets assignment_source) fails inside GroupAssignee.assign/deassign before any outbound task is queued. Those methods do not catch the error, so the webhook errors and assignee updates are not propagated to other integrations either. from_dict() does cls(**input_dict) and does not parse an ISO string back into a datetime, and nothing calls from_dict(to_dict()) or json-round-trips the payload. Eager task tests bypass the broker serializer, so this stays green. Serialize queued with isoformat() and parse it in from_dict.

findings.title: Cycle guard skips every linked issue on the source integration
findings.body: should_sync returns False when sync_source.integration_id matches the target installation's integration, and AssignmentSource does not carry the external issue key that triggered the webhook. sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues one task per GroupLink, but each task then drops outbound assignee sync for the whole integration, not just the ticket whose webhook just ran. A Sentry issue linked to two Jira (or other) issues on the same integration will update Sentry and never push the assignee to the other ticket. That echo is not required to stop the loop: an API update on the other ticket webhooks back, assign/deassign sees no assignee change (affected is false / nothing to delete), and outbound stops. The new test only links one external issue, so this regression is untested.

findings.title: No test that a different integration still syncs outbound
findings.body: test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration only asserts that the same integration's sync_assignee_outbound is not called. There is no case with a second linked integration (or a second external issue on another provider) that must still receive the outbound assign, and no matching deassign case. The guard is if sync_source and ids match: return False. A bug that skipped outbound whenever any AssignmentSource was present would still pass this test, which is exactly the non-regression the PR claims (other integrations must keep propagating). Inbound deassign now passes assignment_source too, and nothing asserts that a same-integration unassign does not echo.
